key_insight: ATSplat brings the adaptive density control of classic 3D Gaussian Splatting into a feed-forward setting by expanding tokens where more geometric detail is needed. This makes compact 3D scene reconstruction less dependent on input image resolution or viewpoint.
problem_solved: Existing feed-forward 3DGS methods usually place Gaussians at input pixels and lift them along camera rays, which ties primitive count and placement to the input view rather than the scene. This paper addresses the loss of scene-adaptive allocation, which limits quality and efficiency.
method: Uses a compact feed-forward architecture that predicts 3D Gaussians from input images.
Introduces adaptive token expansion to increase representation capacity only in under-reconstructed or detail-rich regions.
Avoids strict pixel-aligned primitive generation so the output is more scene-dependent than viewpoint-dependent.
impact: For practitioners, ATSplat offers a more efficient path to high-quality novel-view synthesis with fewer wasted primitives. It is especially useful for applications that need compact, view-robust 3D reconstruction under limited compute or memory.

paper_title: ATSplat: Compact Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting with Adaptive Token Expansion
paper_authors: Cho In, Jeonghwan Cho, Mijin Yoo, Gim Hee Lee, Seon Joo Kim
